A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same paper with readable main text and complete Appendices A–C. Relocated proofs, equations, and tables can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix B.2–B.3 report original matrix and scalar simulations comparing confidence-bound lengths in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: The original matrix and scalar simulation results remain in Section 5.3 and Appendix B.2–B.3, including Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: The paired-variance plug-in bound, self-normalized martingale construction, weighting prescriptions, and classical-variance variant are unchanged. The new covariance example directly applies these existing constructions to outer-product matrices.

E1.justification: Both retain synthetic three-dimensional matrices with independent uniform eigenvalues and scalar uniform simulations. The covariance example introduces no evaluated dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical comparator sets, including original and sharpened Maurer–Pontil and Waudby-Smith–Ramdas bounds in Table 2. Kroshnin and Suvorikova are newly discussed but not included in the simulations.

E3.justification: Both retain alpha = 0.05, the same synthetic generators, sample sizes from 100 to 1,000,000, and confidence-bound lengths normalized by oracle Bernstein bounds. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The scalar sharpening comparison in Appendix B.2 and paired-versus-classical variance analysis in Appendix B.3 are retained. No new ablations, robustness tests, or empirical case studies appear.

E5.justification: Simulation reporting remains unchanged, with no added run counts, seeds, error bars, uncertainty estimates for the reported ratios, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Every numerical entry and ranking in Tables 1–3 is retained. For example, Table 1 reports second-bound/oracle ratios of 1.105 at n = 1,000 and 1.022 at n = 10,000 in both versions.

T1.justification: Example 5.1 adds a formal covariance-estimation application for bounded, zero-mean vectors, deriving the outer-product spectral bound and fourth-moment relationship. Existing theorem statements and proofs remain mathematically unchanged; Theorem 3.1's full proof is relocated to Appendix A.4.

C1.justification: The abstract and summary retain the two sharp-inequality contributions. The introduction qualifies the earlier absence-of-prior-matrix-EB claim by acknowledging a contemporaneous non-sharp result and adds a claim of substantial covariance-estimation benefits.

C2.justification: Example 5.1 explains fourth-moment adaptation and the potential looseness of worst-case covariance bounds. Section 5.2 removes the explicit eigenvalue condition for Minsker's bound to improve on Tropp's and makes the dimension-free open-problem qualification less explicit.

D1.justification: Simulation-generation details, tuning prescriptions, and computational-complexity discussion are unchanged. No implementation resources, hardware details, or code/data-access information are added.

R1.justification: v5 adds Kroshnin and Suvorikova (2024) as contemporaneous matrix EB work and Tropp (2015) for covariance-estimation context. The remaining related-work discussion, including Appendix C, is largely retained.

P1.justification: v5 retitles introductory and method sections, converts preliminary subsections to paragraph headings, and replaces the main-text proof of Theorem 3.1 with a sketch while retaining the full proof in the appendix. Several lemma and corollary cross-references become incorrectly labeled 'Theorem'.

P2.justification: Several displayed equations are compactly typeset, Table 1 moves from page 11 to page 10, and material reflows around the added example and relocated proof. The three tables retain their structures; no figures are added.

improvement.justification: The covariance example clarifies the practical implications of the existing theory, while acknowledging contemporaneous work improves novelty positioning. These limited gains outweigh the new cross-reference mislabels and less precise open-problem wording. The central mathematical guarantees and all simulation evidence remain unchanged.
